newsitem.title: UK: Regulator won't widen review in British Gas row.
newsitem.headline: Regulator won't widen review in British Gas row.

text.p: Industry regulator Ofgas on Monday said it would not ask the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) to investigate "structural changes" at British Gas, but instead focus solely on the controversial price proposals for pipeline unit TransCo.
The regulator added, however, that it might widen the terms of the investigation at a later stage on the MMC's request.
The regulator said last week it was considering broadening the reference after British Gas had rejected Ofgas' final price proposals for TransCo and demanded them to be vetted by the MMC.
Industry watchers feared a wider investigation would hamper British Gas' plan to split itself in two early next year.
British Gas welcomed Ofgas' decision, but the utility retained some reservation as a more extensive MMC reference was not completely ruled out.
"It is good to hear they don't intend to widen it and I hope they won't change their mind later," deputy chairman Philip Rogerson told Reuters.
The utility plans to demerge into British Gas Energy, which will house the trading business and domestic production interests, and a separate company, called TransCo International.
TransCo International would not only include British Gas' regulated transport and storage activities, but also its foreign production and power generation operations.
Press reports had suggested Ofgas might want the MMC to investigate whether the two businesses within TransCo International should in some way be separated.
But an Ofgas spokesman said the regulator considered a wider investigation inappropriate at this stage.
"We've only been dealing with price control and it would be inappropriate to go beyond that at this stage," the spokesman said. "We have no intention of widening the investigation."
Ofgas has asked the MMC to conclude its investigation within six months.
The regulator proposed that TransCo would cut charges to gas suppliers by 20 percent in 1997 and then by 6.5 percent below inflation for the following four years.

British Gas said earlier the proposals would leave it with insufficient money to invest adequately in its infrastructure, adding they would cut the unit's cash flow by 400 million pounds ($631 million). It also feared thousands of job losses if the proposals were implemented.
But Ofgas said the current price regime provided British Gas with more money than it needed to operate its pipelines. ($1=.6337 Pound)
